axes.brief:
Electoral presidential/Assembly selection continues under concentrated executive power, opposition prosecution and weak implementation of judicial constraints. Formal opposition committee membership is assessed against actual obstruction of oversight, and concentrated leadership policy powers against effective independent checks.
Focused six-question reassessment: A personally elected presidency issues emergency decrees subject to formal parliamentary procedures amid weak checks. Constitutional provisions allow specified wartime electoral delay; a governing party cannot freely substitute a president as it could a parliamentary prime minister.
axes.counterEvidence:
Article104 law-over-decree limits, Article105 criminal removal and elections are retained; snap elections are not unilateral postponement and political prosecutions are not a fabricated exclusive presidential ballot veto.
The owner-defined broader axis includes lawful delegation and direct public control; a lower numerical placement is not a regime classification. Six exact responses and response strengths remain inferred. Retained source access dates are not refreshed unless a source was actually revisited. Unchanged answers and other axes were not re-audited. A personally elected presidency issues emergency decrees subject to formal parliamentary procedures amid weak checks. Constitutional provisions allow specified wartime electoral delay; a governing party cannot freely substitute a president as it could a parliamentary prime minister.
